aspects.says: Visa takes purchases as 0100 authorizations through BASE I with BASE II clearing, or as 0200s through its Single Message System.
basis: section:5.3. The MTI and the Processing Code Together Name the Transaction
aspects.reason: orientation about the network that unit 4 already checks through the class digit; name-the-transaction treats both classes alike

aspects.says: On a BASE I link a four-byte prefix and a header come before the MTI; the header's first byte gives its length, and the prefix's length counts the header as well as the message.
basis: section:5.1. On a BASE I Link, a Header Sits Between the Length and the MTI

aspects.says: The class digit says authorization, financial or reversal, the first two digits of field 3 say purchase, cash or refund, and the account digits change neither.
basis: section:5.3. The MTI and the Processing Code Together Name the Transaction

aspects.says: A frame with length zero is a poll, not a message, and VAPChannel writes it back to the network.
basis: section:5.1. On a BASE I Link, a Header Sits Between the Length and the MTI

aspects.says: Some private fields hold a message with its own bitmap; a value set there as text packs on the sender and fails to unpack at the receiver.
basis: section:5.4. A Private Field Can Hold a Message of Its Own, Laid Out by This Release's Specification

aspects.says: A refund is a new credit with its own amount and STAN; a reversal points back at a message whose outcome is still open.
basis: section:5.3. The MTI and the Processing Code Together Name the Transaction

aspects.says: A network reject returns the sender's own message behind a longer reject header, with no field 39; the refusal and its code are in the header.
basis: section:5.2. A Rejected Message Comes Back Behind a Longer Header, With No Field 39

aspects.says: A reject must be recognised before field 39 is read; reported as a decline it hides the field that broke the message.
basis: section:5.2. A Rejected Message Comes Back Behind a Longer Header, With No Field 39

aspects.says: Private-field layouts change with the network's releases, so the packager comes from the current specification and the mapping lives in one component.
basis: section:5.4. A Private Field Can Hold a Message of Its Own, Laid Out by This Release's Specification
aspects.reason: a design recommendation about where code lives; no deterministic test can grade it without the confidential specification
